t: You're on Cheyne Walk, a historic road in Chelsea that runs parallel with the Thames. Before the Chelsea Embankment narrowed the river, the houses fronted the water along the whole length. The painter J. M. W. Turner died here. The novelist Elizabeth Gaskell, author of Cranford and North and South, was born here. The Australian-born artist Mortimer Menpes lived here, and the painter and etcher Walter Greaves was born here too. So was Edward Butler, a linguist and senior librarian at the British Museum. The miser John Camden Neild died on this street.
